framework.name: OWASP Top 10
framework.description: The ten most critical web application security risks.

threats.title: Broken Access Control
threats.description: Restrictions on what authenticated users are allowed to do are not properly enforced.
threats.attackVector: Cookie/parameter tampering to gain admin rights, forced browsing to unauthorized pages.
threats.attackSurface: API endpoints, admin panels, direct object references

threats.title: Cryptographic Failures
threats.description: Sensitive data exposed due to missing or weak encryption, both in transit and at rest.
threats.attackVector: Network sniffing on unencrypted connections, weak cipher downgrade.
threats.attackSurface: Data in transit, data at rest, backups

threats.title: Injection
threats.description: Untrusted data sent to an interpreter as part of a command or query.
threats.attackVector: SQL injection, OS command injection, LDAP injection via unsanitized input.
threats.attackSurface: Form fields, API request bodies, query parameters

threats.title: Insecure Design
threats.description: Missing or ineffective security controls at the design stage, not fixable by implementation alone.
threats.attackVector: Business logic abuse that no amount of input validation can patch.

threats.title: Security Misconfiguration
threats.description: Missing hardening, default credentials, verbose error messages, unnecessary features enabled.
threats.attackVector: Exploiting default admin credentials, directory listing, stack traces leaking internals.

threats.title: Vulnerable and Outdated Components
threats.description: Using components with known vulnerabilities or that are unsupported/out of date.
threats.attackVector: Exploiting a published CVE in an unpatched dependency.

threats.title: Identification and Authentication Failures
threats.description: Weak login, session, or credential-recovery controls letting attackers impersonate users.
threats.attackVector: Credential stuffing, weak password policy, session fixation.
threats.attackSurface: Login forms, session tokens, password reset flows

threats.title: Software and Data Integrity Failures
threats.description: Code and infrastructure that does not protect against integrity violations, e.g. unsigned updates.
threats.attackVector: Insecure deserialization, tampered CI/CD pipeline, unsigned auto-updates.
threats.attackSurface: CI/CD pipelines, serialization boundaries, plugin systems

threats.title: Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
threats.description: Insufficient logging and monitoring lets breaches go undetected for long periods.
threats.attackVector: Attacker actions leave no audit trail to prove what happened.
threats.attackSurface: Application logs, SIEM pipelines, audit trails

threats.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
threats.description: Application fetches a remote resource without validating a user-supplied URL.
threats.attackVector: Attacker-supplied URL causes the server to make requests to internal-only services.
